surtitre: Selective transition to S/4HANA · SAP Activate
titre: A bluefield migration to S/4HANA, from A to Z
intro: The six SAP Activate phases on a timeline. Click a bar, a quality gate or the go-live to open the details.

exemple.description: Alvéa (fictional), food group, two ECC systems merged into a single S/4HANA

chronologieAria: Bluefield transition timeline: SAP Activate phases, steps and quality gates from M-13 to M+2
causesTitre: The 5 most common causes of failure
causes: Dependence on the tool and the expert
Cutover too long for the window
note: Typical approach and indicative durations. Bluefield is the approach whose methods vary most between integrators and transition tools. The example figures are fictional.

s1.s: Keep what works, redesign the rest
s1.obj: Decide to move to S/4HANA while keeping part of the existing landscape and redesigning the rest, with a selective data transfer.
act: Assessment of the current landscape by domain: what works well, what has to change
Comparison of greenfield, brownfield and bluefield
Identifying transformation needs: merging systems, harmonization, reducing history
pre: Clear vision of the domains to transform
Access to the existing systems for analysis
s1.ex: Alvéa, a food group, has two ECC systems inherited from a merger: France and Spain. Production and quality work well, finance and purchasing are inconsistent between the two countries. Choice: bluefield. Production and quality are kept, finance and purchasing are redesigned, and everything is merged into a single S/4HANA, with only five years of history.
ai: Usage analysis by domain to decide what to keep
Comparative summary of the three approaches
r: Bluefield chosen to 'get the best of both' without knowing what to keep: fuzzy project
Decide from Discover, domain by domain, keep or redesign
Cost of tooling and experts underestimated
Estimate the transition tool and expertise in the business case

s2.obj: Get the project up and running, with the tool and expertise for selective transition.
act: Choosing the selective transition tool (SAP or specialist vendor) and its expert
Contracts with the integrator, the tool vendor and the hosting provider
s2.ex: Alvéa selects an integrator and a vendor specialized in selective transition. Process owners are named for each domain, with a simple rule: finance and purchasing will be redesigned, the other domains will be carried over.
r: Three providers with no conductor: integrator, vendor, hosting provider
One person accountable for the transition, RACI signed by all
Dependence on a rare tool expert
Availability clause and a trained backup on the integrator side

s3.s: Readiness Check of the two systems
s3.obj: Measure what the transition demands of each source system.
act: SAP Readiness Check of each ECC
Inventory of custom code and its usage
Comparing configuration between the two systems
s3.ex: The two ECC systems have different charts of accounts, 800 and 1,100 custom objects, and 15 years of history. Production is configured almost identically in both countries.
ai: Automatic comparison of the two systems' configuration
r: Differences between systems discovered in Realize
Compare the configuration from Prepare

s4.s: Which base, which data, which method
s4.obj: Decide how to build the target system and which data to transfer into it.
act: Choosing the target base: converted copy of an ECC without its data (shell), or a new system
Data scope: companies, years of history, objects
pre: Decision on the domains to redesign
s4.ex: The target base is a converted copy of the France ECC, emptied of its data. Data from both countries will be transferred into it, with five years of history. The Spain ECC will then be shut down.
ai: Simulating volumes to transfer according to the history scope
r: Data scope that changes along the way: everything to redo
Scope signed by the business and legal in Prepare
Legal retention obligations forgotten
Have legal and audit validate the history period

q1.obj: Authorize Explore: the transition strategy is settled.
act: Review of the strategy and the data scope
q1.ex: Go-ahead granted. Condition: legal must confirm the five-year history period for both countries.
ai: Consolidating the status of the criteria
r: Explore started without a signed data scope
Scope as a blocking criterion

s5.obj: Confirm domain by domain what is kept, and redesign the chosen domains starting from the standard.
act: Analyzing the S/4HANA changes on the kept domains
pre: Process owners and key users from both countries
s5.ex: Finance: a single chart of accounts for both countries, on the S/4HANA standard. Purchasing: a common standard process. Production and quality: carried over as they are, with only the changes imposed by S/4HANA.
ai: Comparing the processes of the two countries
r: Each country defends its habits: harmonization blocked
Arbitration by the sponsor, standard by default
'Kept' domains drifting toward a redesign
Scope changes only through the change board

s6.obj: Write the rules that select and transform the data during the transfer.
act: Transformation rules: old chart of accounts to the new one, merging duplicate suppliers, renumbering
Converting customers and suppliers into Business Partners
s6.ex: Mapping between the two old charts of accounts and the new one: 2,400 accounts reduced to 900. 6,000 suppliers present in both countries merged into a single Business Partner.
ai: Detecting duplicates between the two systems
s6.own: Data owners, transition team, finance experts
r: Rules written by IT alone: wrong accounting after the transfer
Validation by finance experts and audit
Rules validated too late: empty test cycles
Rules frozen before the first test cycle

s7.obj: Decide the fate of the custom code and design the adaptations.
act: Specifications of the developments in the redesigned domains
s7.ex: Of 1,900 objects, 900 are deleted because they are unused or replaced by the standard in the redesigned domains. 1,000 to fix.
ai: Spotting code that can be replaced by the standard
r: Code in the redesigned domains fixed instead of deleted
Delete by default in the redesigned domains

q2.obj: Authorize Realize: decisions, transformation rules and remediation plan validated.
q2.ex: Finance rules validated by audit. Go-ahead granted.
r: Realize launched with unvalidated finance rules
Finance validation as a blocking criterion

s8.obj: Build the target S/4HANA system, ready to receive the data.
act: Copying the configuration and code of the source ECC, without the data
Technical conversion of this copy to S/4HANA
s8.ex: The base is built from the France ECC in three weeks. It holds the configuration and the code, but no transactional data.
r: Base built on a source that is still changing
Freeze changes on the source, or organize a retrofit

s9.obj: Configure the redesigned domains and fix the code of the kept domains.
act: Sprint-based configuration of the redesigned domains
Adaptations required by S/4HANA on the kept domains
s9.ex: Six sprints for finance and purchasing, with demonstrations to key users from both countries. 1,000 objects fixed in three months.
r: Demonstrations for one country only: the other discovers everything at acceptance
Key users from both countries at every demonstration

s10.obj: Make the selective transfer reliable and bring it within the cutover window.
act: Three or four transfer cycles on production copies
Reconciling amounts and quantities between source and target
s10.ex: Cycle 1: 140 reconciliation gaps, 80 hours. Cycle 2: 25 gaps, 60 hours. Cycle 3: zero gaps, 50 hours, for a 56-hour window.
r: Partial reconciliation: accounting gaps discovered at closing
Full, signed reconciliation at every cycle
First cycle too late
Cycle 1 as soon as the base is ready

s11.s: Regression on one side, new processes on the other
s11.obj: Test the kept domains like a conversion, and the redesigned domains like a new implementation.
act: Regression tests on the kept domains
Integration tests and full acceptance on the redesigned domains
s11.ex: 1,200 regression tests for production and quality, 300 end-to-end scenarios for finance and purchasing. Acceptance signed by both countries.
r: A single test strategy for everything: gaps in the redesigned domains
Two distinct testing approaches

s12.s: Short or full depending on the domain
s12.obj: Train each person according to what changes for them.
act: Short training on the changes for the kept domains
Full training on the new processes for the redesigned domains
pre: Users by role and by country
s12.ex: Two hours for the 500 production and quality users. Three days for the 120 finance and purchasing users, whose processes change.
r: Same training for everyone: too long for some, insufficient for others
Training by domain and by role

q3.obj: Authorize the final preparation: reliable transfer, tested solution.
act: Review of the last transfer cycle
pre: Last cycle with no gaps and within the window
q3.ex: Last cycle with no gaps, in 50 hours. Go-ahead granted.
r: Go-ahead with 'minor' reconciliation gaps
Zero accounting gaps as the criterion

s13.obj: Prepare the production transfer minute by minute.
act: Runbook: shutdown of both ECCs, extraction, transformation, load, reconciliation
s13.ex: Runbook of 520 tasks covering both countries. Rehearsal in 52 hours. Fallback: restart of both ECCs, which stay intact.
r: Two countries, two calendars: poorly coordinated shutdown
A single window, validated by both management teams

s14.obj: Decide, on written criteria, whether to cut over.
r: Go despite reconciliation gaps
Non-negotiable criterion

s15.obj: Transfer the production data and open the new system.
s15.ex: Both ECCs shut down Friday at 6 pm. Transfer in 49 hours. Balances and stock reconciled for both countries. Opening Monday at 6 am.
r: Reconciliation rushed under time pressure
Reconciliation mandatory and signed before opening

s16.s: Stabilize, get through the first closing
s16.obj: Stabilize the system and get through the first joint closing.
act: First closing on the single chart of accounts
s16.ex: Eight weeks. Incidents come mostly from finance, whose process changes. Production, carried over as is, is stable from the first week.
r: Hypercare sized the same everywhere
Reinforcement on the redesigned domains

act: Review of the handover to run
q4.ex: Exit declared eight weeks after go-live.
r: Closure with open incidents
Formal takeover by run

s17.obj: Shut down the old systems and launch what comes next.
act: Archiving the history that was not transferred
s17.ex: History older than five years is archived and stays searchable for audit. Both ECCs are shut down four months after go-live: savings on licenses and hosting.
r: Old systems kept 'just in case': double cost
Shutdown date set in the plan

transverse.obj: Run a hybrid project: steer a conversion and a redesign at the same time.
act: Design authority: boundary between kept and redesigned domains
Risk register, including dependence on the transition tool
pre: Roles and bodies defined from Prepare
transverse.ex: Monthly committee with both countries. Main risk tracked: the quality of the finance transformation rules.
ai: Caution: client data only in a tool approved by the client
r: Keep / redesign boundary that keeps moving
Any scope change goes through the change board
